steps.title: North of Sydney
steps.body: The Hunter Valley lies about 160 km north of Sydney, in New South Wales, along the Hunter River. It's divided into the Lower Hunter, around Pokolbin, the main wine area, and the Upper Hunter. It has about 2,500 hectares of vines. Soils include sandy alluvial flats, good for Sémillon, and red clay on slopes, for Shiraz.

steps.title: Hot and humid
steps.body: The Hunter is one of Australia's hottest, most humid wine regions, and unusually, much rain falls in summer and at harvest, from February to March. Afternoon cloud and sea breezes moderate the heat. The risk of rot at harvest is high, so grapes are often picked early. It's a challenging, sub-tropical climate for vines.

steps.prompt: What is unusual about the Hunter's rainfall?
options: Much of it falls in summer and at harvest

steps.title: History
steps.body: The Hunter is Australia's oldest continuously operating wine region. James Busby, the father of Australian wine, planted vines there in the 1820s and brought hundreds of cuttings from Europe in 1832. Families like Tyrrell, Tulloch and McWilliam's, with Mount Pleasant, have made wine for generations.

steps.prompt: The Hunter Valley is Australia's oldest wine region still in operation.

steps.title: What you learned
points: The Hunter lies north of Sydney, around Pokolbin
It's hot and humid, with rain at harvest
